messages.subject: Calculating the MXLX of light exposure (rather than of physical activity)
messages.subject_clean: Calculating the MXLX of light exposure (rather than of physical activity)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I use GeneActiv and GGIR for my studies and found it really helpful that GGIR supports the estimate of light exposure.
It appears that GGIR by default generates the lux value for the most physically active 5 hours (M5 of PA).
Please can you advise how to calculate the lux for the 5 hours with the most lux value (M5 of light intensity)?

Thank you in advance,
David

messages.subject_clean: Issue with converting activity log into data.frame
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent and Jairo,

first of all, thank you for this great package!

For my study I aim to assess people's level of PA in the 20 minutes before they complete a cognitive test. Hence, I created a log file indicating the segmentation moments (i.e. 20 min. before starting the cognitive test and the moment of starting the cognitive test).

For some days I obtain the correct segments. However, for other days this is not the case. I used the 'g.conv.actlog' function and noticed that there is a problem with converting the log file into date.frame.

For example, line 5 is correct. However, on the other lines the 'testtime' is not taken into account.

 Please find attached the log file.

I use R version 4.3.1 and Windows 10. Thank you for any help you can provide regarding this matter.

Best regards,
Louise

messages.body_plain:
Dear Louise,

Please look at the documentation for the activity log here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/TutorialDaySegmentAnalyses.html#3_Segmentation_guided_by_activity_log:~:text=variables%20across%20days.-,3%20Segmentation%20guided%20by%20activity%20log,-To%20perform%20activity>. GGIR expects an activity log containing one participant per row, with days organized in columns (wide format). You are providing a long-formatted activity log with a different row for every day of measurement for the same participant.

Best,
Jairo

Hi gareth,

I have never tried to process data from different accelerometers at once in GGIR and I would expect compatible results, but it might be that different brands result in different number of columns and, then GGIR cannot combine the part 5 data. For example, processing GENEActiv data could generate LUX-related variables which would not be there in ActiGraph data.

I would suggest to process the ActiGraph and the Axivity data separately, and then you can merge the datasets, for example, using plyr::rbind.fill in R.

Best,
Jairo

Hi Gareth and Jairo,

> Errors and warnings for S03_030_BL (2023-02-22).gt3x.RData$message
> [1] "object 'class.in.ids' not found"

I managed to reproduce the issue, and it is a bug. GGIR is trying to process a window with zero length in the fragmentation analysis. Possible temporary work-around:
Process data without fragmentation
Go to QC folder and look at part 5 daysummary
Identify recordings with zero waking hours, dur_day_min, and omit those from your analysis.
I have created an issue item for it: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/836. I cannot promise to have time for this before the end of August.

>  I get the previously reported error code, I get the following error code, but this is in black, not red (not sure if this makes a difference?).

When GGIR is run serially it is an error in red. You see it in black because you are running the code in parallel, by which the code is only giving you a summary of all the errors that happened in parallel.

> I have never tried to process data from different accelerometers at once in GGIR and I would expect compatible results, but it might be that different brands result in different number of columns and, then GGIR cannot combine the part 5 data. For example, processing GENEActiv data could generate LUX-related variables which would not be there in ActiGraph data.

I intended GGIR to be able to handle multiple accelerometer brands and it did work at some point. If it does not anymore then it would be good to identify when. Even the example Jairo gives with LUX should be handled normally, by leaving the value for those columns empty for recordings without LUX data.

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Erro in part 5
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Erro in part 5
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andreas,

GGIR part 3 and 4 are by default designed to classify sleep based on 5 second epochs. For the alternative sleep algorithms such as Sadeh1994 GGIR is more flexible but there the challenge is that there are insufficient studies to evaluate validity. If you want to classify sleep at a different resolution you should first make sure that sleep detection is meaningful.

This is important, because part 5 heavily depends on meaningful sleep detection part 5.
This is why I implemented the argument part5_agg2_60seconds, which allows you to work with 5 second epochs for sleep but then to aggregate to 60 seconds. We could in theory enhance the code to allow for more aggregation resolutions, e.g. 10, 15, 30, and 60. Although that would require a bit of time investment (support in terms of helping to enhance the code or hiring me to work on this would be appreciated).

The flexibility to choose an epoch length via argument windowsizes was originally designed for part 2 only. For part 3, 4 and 5 it is probably best to stick with 5 seconds and then to consider aggregating to 60 seconds as described above.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Thanks for the detailed description. I am still struggling to reproduce the error.
I processed all csv files directly with your specific GGIR command and did not see an error.
I ran the script based on your output folder and managed to generate the csv reports.
I compared my files inside folder ms2.out with your milestone data and the data is identical.
I am using R 4.3.1 in Windows 11, with all packages up to date.

Are you able to reproduce the error with GGIR argument do.parallel = FALSE? Processing files in parallel should give more elaborate error information. If yes, does that show more details about the origin of the error? If not, type traceback() in the console and share the output of that with us.

many many thanks for your response

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] re-calculating needed for Hildebrand if 30 Hz used as sampling rate?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] re-calculating needed for Hildebrand if 30 Hz used as sampling rate?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Manon,

No correction is needed because metrics like ENMO look at the mean magnitude of the signal, rather than area under the curve or that kind of metrics. So, if we assume the shape of the signal is identical except for the resolution of the data points than mean should be the same.

For other cut-points published in literature this may not be true and you would need to adjust the cut-point accordingly as explained in our vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/CutPoints.html

The above is about the (absence of) interaction between sampling rate and the design of the acceleration metric. Aside from that it is possible that the acceleration the sensor itself produces different output at 30 compared with 60 Hertz, although this influence is likely to be small (ongoing research). ... But even if there would be differences it would be very hard to account for it, because you would need to be able to compare the specific sensors used in that study with your own sensors and from that derive some scaling factor.

Vincent

> Go to QC folder and look at part 5 daysummary
> Identify recordings with zero waking hours, dur_day_min, and omit those from your analysis.

>
> > I have never tried to process data from different accelerometers at once in GGIR and I would expect compatible results, but it might be that different brands result in different number of columns and, then GGIR cannot combine the part 5 data. For example, processing GENEActiv data could generate LUX-related variables which would not be there in ActiGraph data.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part 4: Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2)
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error in part 4: Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2)
messages.body_plain:
Hello Vincent,

I have been looking into the above error a bit and I think I have identified a potential source that may help identify a solution. I narrowed down the source of the issue to be when pulling in the sleep log. I also receive the same error when I run g.loadlog. When I look at the back code for g.loadlog (https://rdrr.io/cran/GGIR/src/R/g.loadlog.R) I see a portion of the code that says:
WKN2 = WKN[1] * 3600 + WKN[2] * 60 + WKN[3]
if (WKN2 > SLN2) { #e.g. 01:00 - 07:00 dur = WKN2 - SLN2 } else <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Control.html> if (WKN2 < SLN2) { #e.g. 22:00 - 07:00 dur = ((24*3600) - SLN2) + WKN2 }
So when I receive the error Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed, It makes me think it may be having an issue with participants that report bed times after midnight and wake times before noon. For example, someone who reports a bed time of 1:00 am and wake time of 7:00 am vs. someone who reports 22:00 - 7:00. To check this, I ran my code only on people who report bed times BEFORE midnight and it was able to run all 5 parts with no error for these people. I'm still unsure how to fix the original error and run it on people who report times after midnight, but I'm hoping this might be able to point us in a better direction.

Thank you again!
Krista

messages.subject: Missing weekend data in Part 5

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am using GGIR package to extract my 24 h physical activity data. I have one participant in Part 2_daysummary output, he completed 6 days, (5 weekdays 1 weekend), this was shown in Part 2 day summary and part 2 summary. The measurement of the device was set at 100 Hz and recorded for 24 hours without fail. We distributed the accelerometer on Saturday and set the device to begin recording at midnight, 00:00 (Sunday). However, on the first day (Sunday), he did not acquire enough hours to be included (12 hours only). He is still included in the analysis because he met our criteria (at least 3 weekdays, and 1 weekend day).

However, as I wish to access his Part 5_daysummary (MM), only weekday data appeared and no weekend data was available, although it was successfully recorded in Part 2 daysummary for MVPA. Is there something wrong with the coding I use? Below is my coding:

Best,
Jairo

I am having similar issues as Marcus with the 2.95 on a new computer. The error is on part 5 using the original gt3x files. The process does not generate a config.csv file. But here is what I am using.
I am using the same code on another computer with the same data and it works.
The major difference between the 2 computers is that the one with the problem is a new installation on a AMD desktop.

the *** is just my local dir

library(GGIR)
GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
      datadir="C:\\***",
      outputdir="C:\\***",
     do.report=c(2,4,5),

     #=====================
     # Part 2
     #=====================
     strategy = 1,

     hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,

     maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
     qwindow=c(0,24),
     mvpathreshold =c(200),
     excludefirstlast = FALSE,
     includenightcrit = 16,
     #=====================
     # Part 3 + 4
     #=====================
     def.noc.sleep = 1,
     outliers.only = TRUE,
     criterror = 4,
     do.visual = TRUE,
      #=====================
      # Part 5
      #=====================
      threshold.lig = c(35), threshold.mod = c(200),  threshold.vig = c(707),
      boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
      boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
      boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
      includedaycrit.part5 = 3/5,
      #=====================
      # Visual report
      #=====================

  timewindow = c("MM"),

      visualreport=TRUE)
And the error.
Part 5 Busy processing ... see C:/DATA/Portugal/test/output_test/meta/ms5.out for progress Error in as.character(Value) : cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type 'character'

Hi,

Can you check if that day appears in the full part 5 report? You'll find that in the QC folder, within the results folder in your output directory. You should get all days in that report, and there you'll probably see the reason why this day is not included in the day report (either the total duration of the day is lower than 23 hours, or the nonwear time during the awake time is higher than 33%).

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Axivity files - Error: "cannot coerce type closure to vector of type character"
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Axivity files - Error: "cannot coerce type closure to vector of type character"
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I think I found the problem. It is related to not having either the GGIRread or the read.gt3x package installed, which generates a new object which cause problem with the config file. I have addressed this in a branch of the GGIR github repository, so you can either install that branch:
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue846_bugCharacterGoogleGroup")

Or you can make sure that you have the packages "read.gt3x" and "GGIRread" installed before running your scripts (I know it might be frustrating having to install packages that you don't need, so feel free to install the branch above instead while this fix is incorporated in GGIR).

Please, let us know if this fixes the error.

Best,
Jairo

Hi All

i am experiencing a similar problem. I have a participant with up to 7 valid days in part 2, however, the participant dissapears in part 5, even no data in the QC folder on that participant. How is this possible?

all the best
Manon

Op woensdag 19 juli 2023 om 08:32:50 UTC+2 schreef Jairo Hidalgo Migueles:

> Hi,
>
> Can you check if that day appears in the full part 5 report? You'll find that in the QC folder, within the results folder in your output directory. You should get all days in that report, and there you'll probably see the reason why this day is not included in the day report (either the total duration of the day is lower than 23 hours, or the nonwear time during the awake time is higher than 33%).
>
> Best,
> Jairo

> > > >

messages.body_plain:
Hello Vincent and all,

I have resolved the issue. I did not realize the AM times needed to have a leading 0 in front (e.g., instead of 1:15:00, it needs to be 01:15:00). Reformatting the times resolved this error.

Thank you,
Krista

On Thursday, July 13, 2023 at 2:59:02 PM UTC-7 Krista Leonard-Corzo wrote:
> Hello Vincent,
>
> I have been looking into the above error a bit and I think I have identified a potential source that may help identify a solution. I narrowed down the source of the issue to be when pulling in the sleep log. I also receive the same error when I run g.loadlog. When I look at the back code for g.loadlog (https://rdrr.io/cran/GGIR/src/R/g.loadlog.R) I see a portion of the code that says:
> WKN2 = WKN[1] * 3600 + WKN[2] * 60 + WKN[3]
> if (WKN2 > SLN2) { #e.g. 01:00 - 07:00 dur = WKN2 - SLN2 } else <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Control.html> if (WKN2 < SLN2) { #e.g. 22:00 - 07:00 dur = ((24*3600) - SLN2) + WKN2 }
> So when I receive the error Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed, It makes me think it may be having an issue with participants that report bed times after midnight and wake times before noon. For example, someone who reports a bed time of 1:00 am and wake time of 7:00 am vs. someone who reports 22:00 - 7:00. To check this, I ran my code only on people who report bed times BEFORE midnight and it was able to run all 5 parts with no error for these people. I'm still unsure how to fix the original error and run it on people who report times after midnight, but I'm hoping this might be able to point us in a better direction.
>
> Thank you again!
> Krista
>

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] cannot open compressed file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Charles,

I see you have commented in several posts with similar issues. I think you are struggling to set up your directory and file paths in your scripts. I suggest you to take some time to revise that the directories and files are well specified in your paths in the GGIR script. Do not change any of the names of the folders produced by GGIR (for example, your output folder and everything that comes inside).

For example, the error described above is triggered when the output directory is not well defined in the GGIR script.

Hope this helps, otherwise let me know.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: calculating physical activity energy expenditure with GGIR package
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: calculating physical activity energy expenditure with GGIR package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jessica and Jairo,

> At the moment there is no algorithm available to calculate physical activity energy expenditure in GGIR.

This is not correct. Several algorithms have been described in the literature to estimate energy expenditure from acceleration metrics that are facilitated with GGIR (I could list some of my own studies for example), but I intentionally did not include any of those algorithms in GGIR, because in my opinion estimating energy expenditure from accelerometer data should be discouraged.

It is something researchers did in the past in order to make data more comparable across sensor brands when each brand had its own magic secret way of calculating movement, but that problem has been largely addressed with raw accelerometry. The only reason we do studies nowadays to look for correlations with energy expenditure is to confirm that the acceleration metrics are still associated with energy expenditure as you would biologically expect.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Hi Vincent,

Thank you for your quick reply.

Your suggestion for installing install R packages read.gt3x and GGIRread worked, thank you.

I have a follow up question regarding time spent in MVPA; I previously set my criteria for LPA, MPA, and MVPA using cut-points derived from Hildebrand 2016 (light: 35.6, moderate: 201.4, and vigorous: 707.0). As I understand, part two should calculate time spent in MVPA, however, in the output files there are multiple variable names. For example, I can see MVPA_E10S_T35.6_ENMO_0.24hr (as I understand there are MVPA based on 10s epoch over 24 hours with the different thresholds, first one being light PA of 35.6 mg), or, would I need to focus on AD_MVPA_E10S_T35.6_ENMO_0.24hr? Just to clarify, which one would be the correct variable for time-spent in LPA?

Thank you for your time and patiences, apologies for any simple questions, I am new to PA analysis! I look forward to hearing from you.

Best wishes,
Samanta

Hi All,

I am currently having the same error cited above and the fix above does not seem to be working for me either.

Here is the error code:  Error in rbind(S, data) : number of columns of matrices must match (see arg 2)

A very limited number of my files have gone through part 1 correctly (running part 1 alone) but these seem to be ones very small in size, the majority of my files will receive the above error.

Any help on how to resolve this would be hugely appreciated.

Thanks,

Daniel

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am PhD student currently analysing some of my Actilife RAW data files collected using the GT9X actigraphs.

I have come across an error when trying to analyse my CSV files on GGIR:

Error in rbind(S, data) : number of columns of matrices must match (see arg 2)

It is strange as some files are still analysing (ones of smaller size) but the majority are not. I have checked this group and saw that a fix was posted for this issue however it does not appear to be working for me if I am implementing it correctly.

I just wondered if anyone else has had problems with this issue or if anyone would be kind enough to direct me on how to fix it.

Many thanks,
Dan

My script:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(
  mode=c(1),
  datadir="removed for personal info",
  outputdir="removed for personal info ",
  do.report=c(2),
  do.parallel=FALSE,
  f0 = 1,
  f1 = 9,
  overwrite=TRUE,
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,
  ndayswindow=7,
  hrs.del.start = 1,
  hrs.del.end = 1,
  maxdur = 18,
  includedaycrit = 10,
  L5M5window = c(0,24),
  M5L5res = 10,
  winhr = c(5,10),
  qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  ilevels = c(0,45,101,429,8000),
  iglevels = TRUE,
  mvpathreshold =c(45, 101, 429),
  boutcriter = c(0.8),            mvpadur = c(1,5,10),
  bout.metric = 4,
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  outliers.only = TRUE,
  criterror = 4,
  do.visual = TRUE,
  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
        boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  visualreport=TRUE)

Jairo

Best,
Jairo

I had this issue using the latest CRAN version of GGIR (2.9-0). Have you tried processing your data using the newest version of GGIR in Git Hub (2.9-5)? This worked for me.

Try:
library(devtools)
install_github("wadpac/GG...@2.9-5")

Best,
Marcus

messages.body_plain:
Hi Zoe,
Your data is in the CSV (Comma Separated Values) format and you want it to be in XLSX (excel table format).
Try searching for "csv to xlsx". It is a simple process and there are several tutorials available.

Best,
Marcus
